item.title: Hakata Ramen School: Make Your Own Ramen — Guide
item.description: For ramen lovers, a Hakata ramen-making class is a fun, hands-on way to get behind the counter of Fukuoka’s most famous dish. Guided by instructors, hands-on experiences let you learn the secrets of tonkotsu ramen — understanding the rich pork-bone broth, preparing the thin Hakata-style noodles, assembling the toppings, and finally cooking and eating a bowl of ramen you made yourself. Some classes are aimed at serious enthusiasts wanting to learn techniques in depth, others are casual, family-friendly experiences; either way you come away with real insight into what makes Hakata ramen special, and the satisfaction of eating your own creation.

item.title: Hakata Tonkotsu Ramen: Fukuoka's Iconic Bowl — Guide
item.description: Hakata ramen is Fukuoka’s most famous dish and the birthplace of tonkotsu (‘pork bone’) ramen, now beloved across Japan and the world. The broth is made by boiling pork bones for hours until rich, creamy and milky-white, deeply savoury and unmistakable. It’s served with distinctively thin, straight, firm noodles that cook in seconds — so you order your firmness (‘barikata’ for very hard is popular), and when your noodles run low you can order a ‘kaedama’, a fresh refill of noodles to add to your remaining broth.

item.title: Fukuoka Food Guide: Hakata Ramen, Mentaiko, Yatai Stalls & More
item.description: Fukuoka is Japan’s greatest food city for its size. In a city of 1.6 million people, the density of excellent, affordable, deeply regional food is extraordinary — from the tonkotsu ramen counters that fill at midnight to the yatai open-air stalls on the Nakasu riverfront, from the morning fresh tuna market at Yanagibashi to the mentaiko tasting counters at Hakata Station. Fukuoka’s food identity is the food of Hakata (the old merchant district of the city): direct, unpretentious, built around pork offal, rich broth, and fermented seafood.
